claims.text: A signed JWT (JWS compact serialization) has three dot-separated parts: Base64url-encoded header JSON, Base64url-encoded payload JSON, and a signature computed over encodedHeader + "." + encodedPayload.
Base64url is a reversible encoding with no key; anyone holding the token can decode the header and payload.
HS256 is HMAC using SHA-256; producing a valid HMAC for changed contents requires the key, so a holder without the signing key cannot make a signature that matches an edited payload.
The exp claim is a NumericDate: the number of seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC.
Jwt:Issuer is "donhang-api" and Jwt:Audience is "donhang-app" in DonHang.Api/appsettings.json at stage-1.
On each request the API recomputes the signature from the received header and payload with its signing key and compares it with the attached one; a mismatch is rejected with 401.

claims.text: Because any holder can read the payload, a payload should hold nothing that must stay hidden from whoever gets hold of the token.
claims.source_hint: follows from claim 5; RFC 7519 section 12 (Privacy Considerations)

claims.text: Base64url is the URL- and filename-safe Base64 alphabet (- and _ instead of + and /, padding omitted), used for JWT parts so they can travel in a URL or an HTTP header.
claims.source_hint: RFC 7515 section 2; RFC 7519 section 1; RFC 4648 section 5

claims.text: Plain base64 -d rejects - and _ and may need = padding; translating with tr '_-' '/+' and padding to a multiple of 4 lets it decode a Base64url part.
